status: PREPARED. NOT APPROVED. NOT EXECUTED. No linear solve has been run on the QMHP mesh for this study. What has run: the solver verification on synthetic cases (solver_verification.json), the QMHP-sized synthetic dry run (dry_run.json), and the QMHP preflight, which refines and assembles but solves nothing (preflight.json).

question.primary: Under nested uniform refinement of the committed mesh (levels 0, 1, 2), does the island capacitance C_h of the meshed model converge at the rate theory predicts? If it does, what limit does that rate imply? The limit comes with a model-based bracket; the one rigorous bound is C <= C_2.
secondary: The same for C'_h, and hence for H_h = 1/((2 pi)^2 L_F C'_h). By the verified sheet-port identity, H_h is Palace's complete harmonic moment on each nested mesh; it is derived, not measured by Palace.
delta_h = C'_h / C_h - 1 on each level: how far Palace's distributed sheet port departs from the declared lumped port in the static moment, since S_h = (1 + delta_h) H_h.
At level 0 only: a cross-code consistency check against the committed L2 band, which is Palace's eigensolver on the same mesh.

A synthetic analogue, not QMHP data. On three QMHP-like cells the C sequence gave R = 2.76, 2.93 (solver_verification.json V2) and 2.60 (dry_run.json): all CONVERGING. configuration.same_space_as_L2_band: The L2 rung's mesh is byte-identical to this mesh (sha256 d8dc1a92...). Its config has order 1, eps 1 and 11.45, LossTan 0, PEC 2 and 4, lumped port 10 in +Y with this L, and UniformLevels 0. Gradients of P1 functions lie exactly in order-1 Nedelec, so level 0 and the L2 band share the discrete space the identity needs.
configuration.refinement: anchor_fem.refine_red: uniform red refinement, every tetrahedron into 8 with the inner octahedron split along its shortest diagonal, every triangle into 4. Applied once for level 1 and twice for level 2. Nested: coarse nodes keep their indices, and midpoints are exact. The level-1 mesh is the one the executed static-anchor test used.
configuration.level_mesh_digest_rule: nested_solver.mesh_digest: sha256 over the canonical little-endian bytes and shapes of xyz, tets, tet_attr, tris and tri_attr. Measured by the preflight; the driver refuses before spending the attempt if a refined mesh differs.
configuration.engine: experiments/static-refinement-study/study_driver.py with nested_solver.py, anchor_fem.py (unchanged) and orchestrator/manifest.py. Independent of Palace. Local; no network, no container, no workflow.

measured_quantities.C_h: Discrete (P1) Maxwell self-capacitance of the island with every other conductor grounded: C_h = eps0 Lc min int eps_r |grad phi|^2 over P1 phi with phi = 1 on the island and 0 on ground. This is the static-anchor quantity, set up with the same expressions.
measured_quantities.C'_h: The same minimum with the port-face potential also held at the linear function of the coordinate along +Y: 0 on the ground end line, 1 on the island end line. Set up exactly as static-band-pairing/spectral.port_constrained_energy.
measured_quantities.H_h: 1 / ((2 pi)^2 L_F C'_h) in GHz^2. By the identity it equals Palace's complete harmonic moment N / sum(p/f^2) = 1 / sum(p/f^2) on the same mesh. The identity requires a rectangular port face whose conductor nodes lie only on its two end lines; this is checked at every level.

independent_variable: The refinement level, 0 -> 1 -> 2. For delta, also the port-face constraint.
controlled_variables: the base mesh and its digest; the refined meshes and their digests
the PEC set and its two-conductor topology
the port face, its direction and its width
the solver settings and the certificate

solvers.level 0: direct: scipy.sparse.linalg.spsolve (SuperLU), the executed record's expressions, for both C and C'
solvers.level 1: direct, as level 0; AND two-grid PCG with level 0 as the coarse space, as an in-run cross-check on the real operator
solvers.level 2: two-grid PCG, with level 1 as the coarse space and the level-1 direct solution prolonged as the initial guess

method.two_grid: nested_solver.TwoGrid: nu forward Gauss-Seidel sweeps; an exact coarse correction with the Galerkin operator P^T A P (SuperLU); nu backward Gauss-Seidel sweeps. P is the P1 prolongation of refine_red restricted to the free nodes. The cycle is symmetric positive definite. It affects only speed; the certificate does not depend on it.
method.stopping: Every check_every iterations the TRUE residual is certified. PCG stops when the relative certificate reaches target_rel (CERTIFIED), after stagnation_checks checks without a 10 % improvement (STAGNATED), on a non-positive curvature (BREAKDOWN), or at maxiter (MAXITER). Anything but CERTIFIED is an integrity failure.
method.certificate: For every energy, direct or iterative: 0 <= E(phi~) - E_h <= sum_i r_i^2 / m_i / (eps_min lambda_1(B)). r is the true residual, bounded componentwise including its floating-point evaluation. m_i = sum of vol/20 over the tetrahedra at node i. B is the mesh's bounding box. The bound requires every outer-boundary node to be constrained, which is checked on every level. The energy's evaluation error is bounded by re-evaluating it in extended precision (x86-64 80-bit long double, required). An inexact solve can only RAISE the energy, so C_h is never understated by the solver. The certificate is relative to the assembled matrix: assembly round-off is common to every solver and is not certified. Proof: nested_solver module docstring.
method.verification_before_any_qmhp_solve: solver_verification.json, synthetic only: V1 exact known answer; V2 two-grid against direct at level 2 on two QMHP-like cells; V3 the certificate holds at every iterate; V4 bit-identity with the reviewed static_capacitance and spectral code, and the dense sheet-port identity; V5 negative controls.

checks: every refined mesh equals its pre-declared digest (checked before the attempt is spent)

on every level: conforming, every boundary face tagged, every outer-boundary node constrained for both problems, and the port face a planar l x w rectangle whose conductor nodes lie only on its end lines (tolerance port_geometry_tol)
exactly two conductors, and the port face bridges them
every energy, C and S present, finite and positive; every bound finite and non-negative
every one of the six primary energies and the two level-1 cross-checks certified to certificate_rel_tol, including the evaluation-error bound
every two-grid solve CERTIFIED, with the Galerkin identity within galerkin_identity_rel_tol and no coarse leak into constrained fine nodes
level 1: the direct and two-grid energies agree within the sum of their bounds
port voltage of the solution equal to 1 within port_voltage_abs_tol, for every solve
C'_h >= C_h and E_{h+1} <= E_h for both problems, within the bounds
C_0 and C_1 reproduce the executed static-anchor record within reproduction_rel_tol
integrity.meaning: Any failure makes the record UNQUALIFIED: no class and no consistency verdict is read from it, though the raw values are preserved. A mesh, band-column, static-anchor-record, pre-declaration or code digest that does not match REFUSES before the attempt is spent.

classification.theory: The energy error of the conforming P1 Dirichlet problem is E_h - E = ||u - u_h||_a^2 >= 0. Every sheet edge carries an r^(1/2) singularity, including sheets lying on the eps interface: the transmission condition keeps the exponent at 1/2. So under uniform refinement the leading term is of order h^1. Vertex singularities are of higher order: for the 90-degree convex plate corner the exponent is about 0.30, a literature value not re-derived here, giving energy order about 1.6. So are smooth terms (h^2). No P1 energy term is faster than h^2. The window below depends only on 1 < q <= 2, not on the vertex value. If X_h = X + a h + b h^q + ... with 1 < q <= 2 and a, b of one sign, then R = d1/d2 lies in [2, 2^q], a subset of [2, 4], and the level-2 error lies between d2/(R-1) and d2. Hence the window and the model-based bracket. The bracket is not a rigorous bound: it assumes the two-term model. The rigorous bound is C <= C_2.

rules.UNQUALIFIED: any integrity failure; for C and C', also a certainly negative difference
rules.NON-CONVERGENT: |d2| >= |d1|: the differences do not shrink. This means no evidence of convergence at these levels. It does not mean mathematical divergence, which the density of nested P1 spaces excludes.
rules.UNRESOLVED: a difference within its certified error of zero; differences of opposite sign that shrink (possible only for delta); 1 < R < R_min (slower than the theoretical leading order); R > R_max (faster than any P1 energy order: pre-asymptotic); or the certified range of R touching 1, R_min or R_max. The last is fail-safe by design: the window's edges are nominally included, but a value that cannot be placed on one side of an edge is not classified. The certified ranges are about 1e-9 relative, so this matters only for a sequence that lands on an edge.
rules.CONVERGING: R_min <= R <= R_max. The limit is reported with its model-based bracket [X2 - d2, X2 - d2/(R-1)], in order, and the level-2 remaining error with the bracket [d2/(R-1), d2] / limit
rules.CONVERGED: CONVERGING, and the conservative remaining error |d2| / |X2 - d2| <= tau_converged

applied_to.C: energies of problem C, with their certified ranges
applied_to.Cprime: energies of problem C', with their certified ranges
applied_to.S: the class of C; S = k / E, with the rigorous lower bound S >= S_2 / (1 + bound)
applied_to.H: the class of C'; H = k / E', with the rigorous lower bound H >= H_2 / (1 + bound)
applied_to.delta: delta_h with its certified range. The sign is free and oscillation is possible, and the rate theory is not derived for delta (both C and C' have leading order 1, so delta generically does too), so its class is descriptive. Also reported: max delta_h, and whether delta_h <= delta_small on every level (S and H agree within 1 %).

C_intervals_given_the_known_C0_and_C1.CONVERGED: unreachable: inside the CONVERGING window the conservative remaining error is at least 0.1215

classification.why_tau_0_05: A conventional engineering tolerance, fixed before any level-2 value exists. The static-anchor windows were factor-2 wide. For C the tolerance is unreachable, as stated above, so it constrains only C' and delta.

consistency_check.what: At level 0, delta_0 = C'_0 / C_0 - 1 (static, this study) against the committed L2 band. The band is Palace's eigensolver on the byte-identical mesh. Two independent codes meet here.

band.rule: All six saved modes; p = |port-EPR| (the sign is Palace's phase convention); sum_p_over_f2 = sum p/f^2; N_B = sum p; f_max = the highest saved frequency.

consistency_check.prediction: Given the identity (N = 1 over all modes, sum_all p/f^2 = 1/H_0 = (1 + delta_0)/S_0) and p >= 0, delta_0 must lie in [delta_band, delta_band + tail], with delta_band = S_0 sum_band p/f^2 - 1 and tail = S_0 (1 - N_B) / f_max^2. The upper end assumes no mode below f_max was missed. With Target 0.5 GHz below the lowest mode, any unsaved mode below f_max would have been closer to the target than mode 6.
consistency_check.eta_derivation: The allowed discrepancy beyond the window, fixed now. Contributions: the band CSVs print 10 significant digits, which bounds the relative error of sum p/f^2 by 1.5e-9; Palace's recorded backward errors are at most 1.6e-11; the static certificates at level 0 are far below 1e-12; LossTan is 0 and Im f / Re f < 1e-9. Total below 4e-9, doubled and rounded up to 1e-8.
consistency_check.window_rule: Recomputed at execution from the pinned band values and the NEW S_0, which the reproduction check ties to the record: [delta_band - eta, delta_band + tail + eta]. CONSISTENT if delta_0's certified range lies inside; INCONSISTENT-LOW or INCONSISTENT-HIGH if it lies wholly below or above; UNRESOLVED if it straddles an edge.
consistency_check.not_an_acceptance_criterion: The check decides nothing about the convergence classes of C, C' or delta, which are static quantities of this study. It decides only whether H_h may be read as Palace's complete harmonic moment on the QMHP mesh. Its window is fixed here from pinned data and a stated error budget, and may not be widened after the result.

consequence.CONSISTENT: The static code and Palace's eigensolver agree on the same mesh within the predicted window. H_h may be read as Palace's complete harmonic moment on the nested meshes, derived through the identity.
consequence.INCONSISTENT-LOW: delta_0 is below what the band data force. This contradicts the identity as applied to Palace's pencil, or the C' implementation on the QMHP mesh. H_h is reported only as the static quantity S'_h, labelled 'identity not confirmed on the QMHP mesh'. The classes of C, C' and delta are unaffected.
consequence.INCONSISTENT-HIGH: delta_0 exceeds the band's bound. Possible causes: a missed mode below f_max, N != 1 for Palace's p, or a mismatch in the p definition. H_h is reported only as S'_h, labelled 'identity not confirmed on the QMHP mesh'. The classes of C, C' and delta are unaffected.
consequence.UNRESOLVED: delta_0's certified range straddles a window edge. H_h is reported as S'_h with the identity unconfirmed.

not_a_target: Agreement with the band, and any class, are outcomes and not targets. Nothing in the computation of C_h or C'_h reads the band, the executed record's values or the expected classes. The tolerances, windows and rules above were fixed before any C_2, C'_h or delta_h value existed, and may not be changed after one does.
no_combination: C_h, C'_h, S_h, H_h and delta_h must not be combined with the conditional Route A coupling g, the readout frequency f_R or any Route A output. No E_C,F1F1 is reported; it stays UNAVAILABLE.

budget.retry: none. A failure, a refusal after the record exists, a timeout, a budget limit or an integrity failure is the recorded outcome.
budget.enforcement: In the process, from the moment the record directory exists: RLIMIT_CPU soft (raises, and is recorded) with a kernel kill 60 s later; RLIMIT_AS (an allocation beyond it fails, and is recorded); SIGALRM at the wall cap (raises, and is recorded). Python handles signals between bytecodes, so the invocation also carries an outer hard kill 60 s beyond the wall cap.
budget.invocation: from the repository root, locally, no workflow, no network: timeout --signal=KILL 3660 .venv/bin/python experiments/static-refinement-study/study_driver.py

estimate.basis: dry_run.json: the exact execution path under this budget, on a QMHP-sized synthetic stand-in LARGER than the QMHP ladder (level 2: 4,999,680 tets and 791,574 unknowns, against 4,123,776 and 584,914) with WORSE elements (aspect p50/p99 5.0/25.1, against 4.7/14.2).
estimate.expected_on_the_qmhp_ladder: about 3-5 min wall, 5-8 min CPU, 4-5 GB resident, below 8 GB address space, if PCG needs a comparable iteration count. The iteration count on the real mesh is not known until the run; the level-1 cross-check reports it on the real operator.
estimate.worst_case_within_the_settings: maxiter = 1000 on every PCG solve: about 60 s (levels 0-1 direct) + 2 x 50 s (level-1 cross-checks) + 2 x (27 + 360) s (level 2), about 16 min wall and 26 min CPU. The stagnation rule normally stops a failing solve well before that. Either way the result would be recorded as an integrity failure, not retried.
estimate.why_these_caps: cpu 60 min and wall 60 min cover the worst case with a margin of about 2; the 12 GB address-space cap is 1.6 times the stand-in's peak on a 15 GB machine.

stop_conditions: any refusal, failure or integrity failure: record it and stop
